subject: Demo snapshot and pilot proposal — Bluecrest Health
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@bluecresthealth.com>, Leah Simmons <leah.s@bluecresthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo snapshot and pilot proposal — Bluecrest Health

Hi Daniel & Leah,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — really appreciated the candid discussion about your triage workflow and the latency/cost sensitivities on overnight batches. Below is a short recap of what we showed and a proposal for a focused pilot that should get you to a decision within 6 weeks.

Demo snapshot (what we covered)
- High-level: Redwood inference runtime, routing to lower-cost quantized variants, and prefix caching for repeated triage queries.
- Live demo: 2-minute cold start vs warmed KV-cache for a 1,500-token clinical note (we saw 35% token-cost improvement with caching).
- Integration options: API + SFTP batch ingests for nightly throughput, or a streaming endpoint for near-real-time triage.

Proposed pilot: Bluecrest 6-week validation pilot (goal: validate accuracy & unit-cost for nightly triage)
- Scope: Run 100k nightly notes through Redwood private (VPC) in staging; compare Redwood outputs to your current heuristic labels for precision/recall and per-case latency.
- Success criteria (pass/fail gates):
  1) Precision >= 92% for top-1 triage label on the test sample;
  2) Median end-to-end latency per note (batch window) <= 1.2s;
  3) Token cost <= $0.007 per note for the chosen model/profile;
  4) No PII leakage observed in logs and KMS-backed key access for any stored artifacts.
- Timeline (target)
  Week 0 (kickoff): environment access + dataset handshake
  Week 1–2: model selection, integration (SFTP/ingest) and smoke runs
  Week 3–4: full nightly runs, adjust batching/quantization tuning
  Week 5: evaluation, quality review, cost analysis
  Week 6: executive review and next-step recommendation
- Owners
  - Bluecrest: Daniel (product owner), Leah (security lead)
  - Redwood: Sofia (AE, engagement lead), Ben (SE, technical lead), Marissa (CS, success plan)
- Deliverables
  - Pilot run plan + acceptance checklist (attached: Bluecrest_Pilot_Scope.xlsx)
  - SOW draft for production (attached: SOW_Bluecrest_v1.docx)

Requests / asks from Bluecrest to start (quick wins)
1) Share a 1–2 day sample (SFTP or secure share) and a schema for labels + approximate nightly volume.
2) Confirmation on the minimum legal PII redaction requirements for logs and a contact for your security questionnaire.
3) Decision on which integration mode you prefer (SFTP batch vs streaming API).

If this aligns, I can lock in a kickoff for Monday 12th at 10am PT and loop in engineering for the environment setup.

Thanks — Sofia
--
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Demo snapshot and pilot proposal — Bluecrest Health

Thanks Sofia — great session. A few clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Success criteria: the precision bar of 92% seems reasonable for top-1 labels, but we need to ensure recall on high-risk triage codes (the ones flagged as 'urgent') stays above 88% — can Redwood include that as a sub-metric?
2) Data: We can share a 48-hour dump next week; however, PHI constraints mean we must not send raw identifiers. We'll provide a redacted sample and a mapping key under NDA.
3) Security questionnaire: Leah will own that, but she'll need a point of contact on your side.

We like the 6-week cadence — can you confirm the proposed weekly checkpoints (short sync + metric milestone)? Also, the timing for kickoff on Mon 12th conflicts with a clinical all-hands; can we move to Tue 13th 11am ET (8am PT)?

Daniel
Product Lead, Bluecrest Health
D: 617-555-0220

1) Metrics: yes — we'll add the high-risk recall gate (>= 88%) and provide a short per-code breakdown in the Week 5 evaluation report.
2) Data sharing: redacted dump is fine. We'll send an NDA addendum for the mapping key and accept SFTP with encrypted keys. Ben will take point on the ingestion spec.
3) Security contact: Marissa will be the primary contact for the questionnaire (cc'd). She'll share our SOC2 summary and a short technical note on log redaction and KMS.
4) Kickoff: Tue Mar 13, 2028 at 11:00am ET / 8:00am PT works for us — locking that in and sending a calendar invite.

Next steps (action items)
- Sofia: send calendar invite + kickoff agenda (today EOD)
- Ben: upload ingestion spec + SFTP instructions to the Drive link (by Mon EOD)

I'll also attach a compact acceptance checklist to keep the pilot gating clear. Please review and flag anything missing.

Best,

Morning all — Ben here (SE). Quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff and a short checklist for Daniel/Leah so we can hit the Week 1 smoke tests quickly.

Technical checklist
- SFTP sample: 2 files (schema + 48-hour redacted sample) with filename convention and a short README. Please use the temp SFTP credentials we'll provide and rotate the keys after ingestion.
- Ingest schema: CSV/JSON fine; include a stable id, text payload, and label columns. No direct patient identifiers in the payload. If you must include mapping keys, ship them under NDA only.
- Compute profile: we'll start with a 4-GPU equivalent q4_8bit profile; if nightly throughput hits >150k notes we will scale to dedicated pools.
- Security docs: please attach the completed questionnaire (Leah) to the Drive folder — Marissa will confirm receipt and next steps for any outstanding items.

I'll post the ingestion spec to the shared Drive (link below) and a short runbook for running the local smoke tests. If you can share the 48-hour sample by Mon 5pm ET, I can validate ingestion by Tue morning and have the first sample runs ready for Wed.

Runbook & attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CdefPilotDocs

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
